FALSE POSITIVES

By: Jana Marx | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Tonight on Carte Blanche we're proving that it's not that difficult to trick a breathalyzer or drug test into giving false positive results - results that could leave uninformed employees jobless.

Unique Selling Point:
We're going to do our own experiments in a real science lab! The whole crew will participate in testing different foods, bevereges and household products to see how easy it is to trick a breathalyzer and preliminary drug test.

Summary:
The sight of a roadblock fills most of us with dread, even if we have nothing to hide…Alcohol testing just puts people on edge. But it’s not only at roadblocks where you’ll find breathalysers. In industries like mining, construction, public transport..in fact, wherever heavy machinery is operated, safety dictates that the day starts with a negative test for employees. This also goes for drug tests. Now, this sounds all good and well and essential, but what if you test positive for alcohol or drugs, when you had no substances or alcohol? What if tests can be fooled by the household products you use, the food you eat and even the diet you are following? We experiment with different products to test what science found: That the preliminary or screening testing devices are notoriously unreliable and can be "tricked" into giving false positives. This may very well cause people to lose their jobs - those in the most trouble, the disenfranchised worker who doesn't know their rights.

Script:


1: The sight of a roadblock fills most of us with dread, even if we have nothing to hide… Alcohol testing just puts people on edge.

2: But it’s not only at roadblocks where you’ll find breathalysers. In industries like mining, construction, public transport..in fact, wherever heavy machinery is operated, safety dictates that the day starts with a negative test for employees.

3: A young man we call Simphiwe worked at a sawmill in the KwaZulu-Natal Midlands.It was November 2020 - just another work day like every other.

4: Simphiwe UPS 04;13 We were chatting along the way to work. My friend remarked that the breathalyzers were making beeping sounds and read positive even when no one was touching it.

5: But Simphiwe knew the drill: A sawmill is no place for drunk employees and after 10 years on the job, he was used to the daily test.

6: Simphiwe UPS 04;20 -04;30 When I arrived at the gate, the security guard told me to blow into the breathalyzer. I asked him: “Do you trust this machine?” He still made me blow.

7: That morning Simphiwe tested positive for being under the influence at work. It made no sense to him.

8: Simphiwe UPS 05:48 05;51 I saw this incident as bad luck, because I really didn’t drink any alcohol.

9: He insisted that he only had three fat cakes and an energy drink for breakfast.

10: Hot cross bun video intro: “Can you see, it’s zero zero zero…

11: In 2019, two traffic officers caused a social media storm when they ate hot cross buns and tested positive for alcohol on a breathalyzer.

12: Breathalyzers come to play in criminal cases like driving under the influence, and in the workplace. The legal limit on the road is 0.05 g in 100 mL of blood. That’s about one beer. In the workplace the employer decides on the permissible limit - it’s usually zero.

13: LAB LINK Serious discrepancies have been raised about breathalysers in the workplace, calling into question their scientific accuracy.

14: Dr Tim Laurens has been working as a Forensic Toxicologist for more than 30 years. He’s an expert in alcohol and drug testing and he’s found breathalyzers used at a roadblock or in the workplace notoriously unreliable.

15: DR LAURENS UPS 23;42 Are Breathalyzers…can we trust them? That would be the biggest mistake you can make in my opinion. 3;35 Remember, the zero level differs from one device to another device. It depends on the quality, so we're not even sure what zero is…

16: Dr Laurens says the devices can be fooled by a number of different foods, beverages, medicine and household products.

17: DR LAURENS UPS 1;19 Breathalysers are subject to interferences and these interferences can be residual alcohol in the mouth, or it can be alcohol in the environment or it can perhaps be alcohol on the person who holds the breathalyser on his hands, maybe due to sanitizer.

18: Our crew decided to do our own experiments, to see how easy it was to trick a breathalyzer.

19: SOUND from the chats between crew
We made sure no one had anything in their bodies that would compromise the tests.


20: With everyone in the clear, we were set to experiment with hot cross buns, an energy booster, mouthwash and cough medicine.

21: (Claire tests)

22: 0.39 - 0.44 “That - you are in an alcohol coma.”

(Claire then laughs)

23: According to a guideline by Arrive Alive, a reading that exceeds zero point four means the individual suffers from alcohol poisoning. It can be fatal.

24: The traces of alcohol in my breath will disappear after a few more minutes. But at this moment, I’m in big trouble.

25: Our producer took cough mixture before blowing into the Breathalyzer.
26; Although she is not breaking the law, the little alcohol in the medicine could get her fired from work. Most employers have a zero-tolerance alcohol policy.

27: DR LAURENS UPS 1;21 You must keep in mind that employers have an obligation according to the Occ-Health and Safety Act, that people must be operating safely in the work environment.

28: Our camera assistant took an energy booster sachet.

29: If he was working in the transport sector, he’d be jobless after exceeding the legal limit of zero point zero two grams per 100 mL of blood for professional drivers.

30: As we were nearing lunch, our cameraman was only too happy to test the hot cross buns.

31: Had he worked on a mine, it could’ve led to disciplinary action.

32: Yeast is the main culprit…it ferments in the baking process, creating residual alcohol in the buns.

33: Even following the keto diet can get you into trouble! Dr Laurens says the diet causes ketone bodies to be produced by the liver that form compounds similar to alcohol.

34: DR LAURENS UPS 10;22 and one of them is acetone, for instance. So if you would have acetone it is metabolised or changed by the body to isopropanol. So, it's very similar to alcohol.

35: So, stay away from yeast and alcohol, right? But what if there’s no way of knowing if there’s alcohol in a drink?

36: We waited for the cameraman’s mouth-alcohol to disappear, and then gave him an alcohol-free energy drink.

Wimpie says: Okay, I’m ready…

37: The result was worth a mic drop…

38: There’s no way for us to know what triggered that false positive. But all of these preliminary positive results could have been ruled out by a second test.

39: DR LAURENS UPS 1;52 So, a preliminary test is normally just what it says - a preliminary test - and it needs to be confirmed. 1;45 The same procedure would apply for drug testing, for instance, a preliminary drug test, when you have a preliminary assay, with devices like this, where you you collect the urine, and you have a preliminary assay. 1;58 And how is it then confirmed? The confirmation test involves a procedure as well as a technological device.

40: Simphiwe’s employer didn’t send him for a confirmation test and he was fired.
41: “Seinfeld” link: Claire stands next to the oven and watch this scene in Seinfeld on the laptop:
(Elaine: Mr. Peterman, I don't know what's going on here. I am not addicted to anything.
Peterman: Oh, Elaine…)
Now, you might remember that episode of “Seinfeld” where Elaine is called into her boss’ office because she failed a drug test for opium.
She soon discovers that the reason was the poppy-seed muffins she often enjoyed.

42: As funny as that episode of “Seinfeld” is, there is nothing funny about failing a breath or drug test because of the food you ate.

43: Some US employees even resorted to what's now become known as the “Seinfeld Defence”, to fight unfair dismissal following positive drug tests.

44: Our producer ate four muffins over the course of 12 hours. At 5 pm, she tested positive for opioids. That includes prescription drugs such as codeine and morphine, and illegal drugs like heroin.

46: DR LAURENS UPS 14;46 So now, if you're not careful, we can make all sorts of accusations against this worker now.

47: CCMA LINK: Without the legal muscle to challenge these dismissals, disenfranchised workers lose their jobs with little to no chance of re-employment after being fired for being under the influence at work.

48 Legal experts have long understood the shortfalls in legislation when it comes to using breathalyzers - especially in the workplace. Kgomotso Mufamadi is an attorney and lecturer at the University of Johannesburg.

49 : KGOMOTSO UPS 2:28 - 2:33. So just testing positive for alcohol on a breathalyzer 2:35 is not sufficient to dismiss someone? 2:38 - 2:42: In and of itself won't be sufficient. 5:21 - 5:34 Ideally, it would take quite a lot of other factors, for example, is this the first time the employee has come to work under the influence of alcohol, or the other misconduct that the employee has committed?

51: Dr Llewelyn Curlewis, a criminal lawyer and senior lecturer says there’s no legislation forcing employers to send employees for confirmation tests.

52: LLEWELYN UPS 15:01 You sit with the situation that the employer must merely prove 51% to get a conviction and to dismiss that employee.

53: The low burden of proof for employers makes new legislation critical to improve the fate of innocent workers.

54: LLEWELYN UPS 24:51 Legal experts, obviously our parliamentarians 25:02 and scientists, 25;08 must sit together, formulate proper protocol that must be incorporated in legislation.

55: LLEWELYN 18:04 - 18:08 All we say is have protocols in place to ensure that there's always 18:10 a confirmatory test done.

56: We’ve been told some people get arrested at roadblocks after only a preliminary test.

57: But Superintendent Michael Botolo from the Johannesburg Metro Police Department or JMPD says this is wrong and insists that proper procedure must be followed.

58: Botolo UPS: 0;37 You will gargle a little bit with the mouthwash? Yes. Okay cool. 01;12 The operator will hold a breathalyzer and we’ll request the subject to open a mouthpiece and explain the procedure thereof…the next phase it will be the EBAT machine.

59: The EBAT or evidentiary machine rules out any trace of alcohol that might have fooled the preliminary device.

60: The mouthwash causes a positive reading on the preliminary breathalyzer.

61: But after 15 minutes the officer is tested on the more sophisticated device.

62: JMPD UPS: 0;25 Ah, look at that!

JMPD: What did I tell you?

Mouth alcohol.

JMPD: So now we know that it's not ethanol. It's the alcohol that is in the mouth.

63:But this information would be cold comfort for the young father from KwaZulu-Natal who lost his job so unceremoniously.

64: Simphiwe UPS 00;29 -00;47 There are things, many things, I can’t do anymore – like paying school fees. But when I do piece jobs, I can at least buy groceries and food.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Tonight on Carte Blanche we're proving that it's not that difficult to trick a breathalyzer or drug test into giving false positive results - results that could leave uninformed employees jobless.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We're going to do our own experiments in a real science lab! The whole crew will participate in testing different foods, bevereges and household products to see how easy it is to trick a breathalyzer and preliminary drug test.
metadata.Summary: The sight of a roadblock fills most of us with dread, even if we have nothing to hide…Alcohol testing just puts people on edge. But it’s not only at roadblocks where you’ll find breathalysers. In industries like mining, construction, public transport..in fact, wherever heavy machinery is operated, safety dictates that the day starts with a negative test for employees. This also goes for drug tests. Now, this sounds all good and well and essential, but what if you test positive for alcohol or drugs, when you had no substances or alcohol? What if tests can be fooled by the household products you use, the food you eat and even the diet you are following? We experiment with different products to test what science found: That the preliminary or screening testing devices are notoriously unreliable and can be "tricked" into giving false positives. This may very well cause people to lose their jobs - those in the most trouble, the disenfranchised worker who doesn't know their rights.
